newsitem.title: GERMANY: Dispute seen brewing within Daimler over revamp plans.
newsitem.headline: Dispute seen brewing within Daimler over revamp plans.

text.p: Daimler-Benz AG on Friday appeared to be on a collision course with the management of its flagship automotive subsidiary Mercedes-Benz AG over a proposed management revamp.

Sources close to Germany's largest industrial group said the management of Mercedes, headed by Chief Executive Helmut Werner, opposed a reported plan by Daimler chief Juergen Schrempp to integrate Mercedes fully into Daimler.
A report in local newspaper Stuttgarter Zeitung said Werner, whose position would effectively be made redundant by the move, had threatened to resign if the plan went ahead.
There was no official comment from the companies, which issued a statement reiterating that the group was discussing a reorganization to make its management structure more efficient.
"Insofar as the media link this with speculation about personnel, we do not comment on that as a rule," it said.
Sources close to Daimler had said on Thursday that Daimler was considering a plan under which Mercedes would be merged with the parent company.

The plan is seen as part of a drive by Schrempp to take Daimler back to its roots as a transportation group, reversing the move by his predecessor Edzard Reuter to create an integrated technology holding group.

Following the dissolution earlier this year of its loss-making AEG industrial division and the bankruptcy of the majority-held Fokker Dutch plane-maker unit, analysts said such a move would be viewed as a logical next step.

Sources close to Daimler believe that an internal "merger" of the Mercedes-Benz car- and truck-making unit, which now makes up around three-quarters of its group revenues, would also likely be accompanied by management changes.
